review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for other uses of leftAdd/rightAdd/SemiadditiveOfBinaryBiproducts. All uses are inside this file. I did not run Lean, so the simp-set effects are inferred from the source and not observed. The local add_comp/comp_add lemmas are stated for a local instance, so leaving them non-simp looks correct. The only finding is a low-to-medium confidence one about the simp attributes on the two defs.

findings.problem: Both auxiliary definitions carry a global `@[simp]`, so every simp call that imports this file unfolds `leftAdd`/`rightAdd` to `biprod.lift … ≫ biprod.desc …`. They are scaffolding for building the `AddCommMonoid` instance, and their notation is `local`. The attribute is also not what the proofs use. The proofs write `simp [hr f, leftAdd, …]` and `rw [leftAdd, h₁, …, rightAdd]`, and `leftAdd`/`rightAdd` are listed explicitly in the simp sets at lines 65, 66, 81 and 82. Either the attribute or the explicit unfolding is redundant. The attribute also makes the simp set depend on an implementation detail. The intended normal forms are only meaningful for the local `AddCommMonoid` instance, which comes from `add_eq_right_addition` and `add_eq_left_addition`. Those two lemmas are deliberately not simp, which is sensible.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `leftAdd` and `rightAdd`. The proofs already pass `leftAdd`/`rightAdd` explicitly to `simp` and `rw`, so they should still go through, though I have not compiled this. If the attribute is kept, drop the redundant explicit `leftAdd`/`rightAdd` arguments from the `simp [...]` calls and document why the defs are simp.
findings.benefit: Downstream simp sets no longer unfold these private-in-spirit helper definitions. The simp interface of the file is then explicit: the helper defs are unfolded only where the proofs ask for it, and the local `+` instance is untouched.
